resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM Status=construction corroborated. wattaennews (Wattan News Agency, 2024-09-23) headline 'تقدم كبير في إعمال ربط خط أنبوب الغاز بزركان حلفاية' (significant progress in the connection works of the Bazargan-Halfaya gas pipeline), with the Maysan Oil Co. gas-dept director quoted that 'there is significant progress in the pipe-connection works, executed by a contractor to which the project was assigned.' Wayback-archived iraq-businessnews (2025-03-18, sourcing INA) states '80% progress has been made on a 60-kilometer gas pipeline linking Buzurgan to Halfaya.' Also independently supported by al-mirbad (2023-05-26): implementing company had begun site handover, topographic and pipeline-route survey. Two+ independent reports at different dates -> under construction. tier high. (Original current_ref iraq-businessnews 2024 article now returns HTTP 401 behind a bot-wall -> not stageable; its Wayback copy verifies but I staged fresher/independent corroboration.)

Fuel=Gas confirmed. Every source describes a gas pipeline: wattaennews 'خط أنبوب الغاز بزركان حلفاية' (Bazargan-Halfaya gas pipeline), Wayback iraq-businessnews 2024 'the 18-inch gas pipeline between Bazargan and Halfaya.' Two independent working sources. tier high.

PipelineType=transmission corroborated. al-mirbad (2023) explicitly 'مد الأنبوب الناقل من البزركان إلى حقل الحلفاية' (laying the transmission/carrier pipe from Bazargan to Halfaya field); wattaennews describes it as part of 'خطوط الأنابيب النفطية التابعة لوزارة النفط' (the Oil Pipelines Company network under the Ministry of Oil) carrying field gas ~70 km to power plants. A field-to-power-plant transmission line, not a distribution/gathering line. Two independent sources. tier high.

Capacity=70 MMcf/d corroborated. wattaennews (2024): Maysan Oil Co. supplies surplus gas 'بكمية تترواح من (٦٠ إلى ٧٠) مقمق' (60-70 MMscf/d). Wayback iraq-businessnews (2025, sourcing INA): 'gas compression unit with a processing capacity of up to 70 million standard cubic feet per day (MMscf)' and elsewhere 'a gas compression unit with a processing capacity of 50-70 MMscf.' GEM's 70 sits at the top of the reported range; both sources agree on 70 as the figure. Two independent reports months apart. tier high (minor note: sources give a 50/60-70 range, GEM uses the 70 ceiling).

Diameter=18 in corroborated by one source: Wayback-archived iraq-businessnews (2024-07-24), quoting Deputy Minister of Oil for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber on 'the 18-inch gas pipeline between Bazargan and Halfaya' (Source: Ministry of Oil). Only one origin found (the Ministry-of-Oil statement, republished by iraq-businessnews; live page 401s so the verified Wayback copy is staged). Arabic searches for a diameter (قطر ١٨ بوصة/انج) did not surface an independent second source. tier medium, single origin.

FuelSource=Bazargan Field corroborated. Both sources: a gas compressor unit (GCU) is installed 'في حقل البزركان' (in the Bazargan field) to capture associated gas produced there, which is then piped to Halfaya. wattaennews and al-mirbad are independent (2024 vs 2023). tier high.

Location Bazargan -> Halfaya (Maysan, Iraq) corroborated. al-mirbad (Maysan Oil Co. statement): 'مد الأنبوب الناقل من البزركان إلى حقل الحلفاية' (pipe from Bazargan to Halfaya field), in Maysan governorate. wattaennews: Bazargan-Halfaya line within Maysan Oil Company fields. Wayback iraq-businessnews also 'between Bazargan and Halfaya,' tagged Maysan/Missan. Both fields are in Maysan (Missan) province, Iraq. Two+ independent sources. tier high.

Owner=Iraq Ministry of Oil (100%) corroborated at the ministry level. wattaennews: the line is 'ضمن خطوط الأنابيب النفطية التابعة لوزارة النفط' (part of the oil-pipelines network belonging to the Ministry of Oil) and 'المشروع العائد اساسا لشركة خطوط الأنابيب النفطية' (the project belongs to the state Oil Pipelines Company); Maysan Oil Company is the gas supplier. Wayback iraq-businessnews: statement by the Deputy Minister of Oil, 'Source: Ministry of Oil.' The specific state entities (Oil Pipelines Co. / Maysan Oil Co.) are all under the Iraq Ministry of Oil, so GEM's owner is consistent. Two independent sources. tier high.
